title: Daily news update — Monday to Friday, 5–9 October 2026

articles.title: Russian attack kills 6 in Ukraine's Kharkiv, shatters residences
articles.summary: Regional authorities said nearly 60 people were injured after three bombs struck different areas of Kharkiv.

articles.title: Russia says it launched 'massive' strikes on Kyiv, other areas of Ukraine
articles.summary: Russia’s defence ministry said the targets included missile and drone facilities in Kyiv and sites in several other regions.

articles.title: Ukraine says it hit Russia's largest oil refinery
articles.summary: The military said the Omsk facility, around 2,500 km from Ukraine, is operated by Gazpromneft and supplies fuel to the Russian army.

articles.title: Yemen's Houthis say they attacked Riyadh airport with ballistic missile
articles.summary: Saudi Arabia had reported that an earlier attack on the same airport killed one person but had not confirmed the new Houthi claim.

articles.title: Hormuz transits at lowest in over two months after attacks, data shows
articles.summary: Kpler counted seven commodity vessels crossing on Tuesday, the fewest since 23 July, after tanker attacks reached a wartime weekly high.

articles.title: Attack risks rise for tankers as Iran vows to block more Hormuz routes
articles.summary: Iran warned it would block shipping routes it had not authorised after the heaviest week of tanker attacks since the war began.

articles.title: Vessel struck by unknown projectile off UAE coast amid surge in attacks, UKMTO says
articles.summary: The strike caused a fire that was extinguished, while authorities investigated the condition of the crew and the damage.

articles.title: Kapidzic Announces New Majority in Sarajevo: SDA, SBiH and DF Begin Government Formation
articles.summary: The SDA, SBiH and DF said they held 18 seats in the Sarajevo Canton assembly and expected to gain a 19th.

articles.title: Vice President of RS on Election Results: Bosniaks Are Politically Marginalized in Republika Srpska, We Lost the Protection Mechanism
articles.summary: Duraković said new voting technologies improved transparency but alleged that vote buying remained a problem.

articles.title: Ukraine scrambles for money to fight war as Russian strikes batter economy
articles.summary: Russian strikes halted a major steel plant and mines in Kryvyi Rih as the government faced its largest budget crisis since the invasion.

articles.title: Russia says Ukraine hit two facilities at Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant
articles.summary: Rosatom chief Alexei Likhachev said a food delivery driver was killed and two facilities were hit, while stating there was no threat to nuclear safety.

articles.title: Rubio says war in Ukraine is at a dangerous stalemate
articles.summary: Speaking in Lisbon, the US secretary of state said Washington would keep seeking a permanent negotiated settlement.

articles.title: Iran is now ‘satisfied’ with Trump Route, Armenia Foreign Minister says
articles.summary: Ararat Mirzoyan made the statement after visiting Tehran, which had earlier warned about a possible US military presence near its border.

articles.title: Production starts in Azerbaijan’s first Israeli weapons factory
articles.summary: Israeli firm ARI Arms is producing M-4 type rifles in a joint venture involving the two countries’ defence ministries.

articles.title: Azerbaijan students launch school strike over hijab restrictions
articles.summary: Pupils at two schools boycotted classes over restrictions affecting classmates who wear the hijab.

articles.title: Georgian singer alleges police assaulted him and pressured him to confess to crimes
articles.summary: The Interior Ministry disputed Misho Sulukhia’s account, saying police stopped him after he refused an order and fled.

articles.title: Kobakhidze to EU: Moldova and Ukraine are only ahead of Georgia ‘in negative indicators’
articles.summary: His remarks followed EU Enlargement Commissioner Marta Kos’s statement that she wished Georgia were at Moldova and Ukraine’s level on EU integration.

articles.title: ‘They beat us’: More inmates claim abuse from staff as Georgia’s prisoner protests continue
articles.summary: The inmates said they were protesting in solidarity with a prisoner who accused guards of rape; the penitentiary service denied the allegations.

articles.title: Kazakhstan Defense Ministry Inspection Leads to 13 Criminal Cases in Wake of Soldiers’ Deaths
articles.summary: The inspection followed the deaths of 14 servicemen during Caspian Sea exercises and found failures in planning and safety measures.

articles.title: Central Asian countries agree on reservoir operations for 2026-2027
articles.summary: At an Interstate Commission for Water Coordination meeting in Turkmenbashi, members agreed water withdrawal volumes and reservoir schedules for the 2026–27 non-growing season.

articles.title: Kyrgyzstan Court Jails Kadyr Atambayev and Temirlan Sultanbekov
articles.summary: Kadyr Atambayev received four years and opposition leader Temirlan Sultanbekov seven over an alleged post-election power-grab plot; both denied the charges.

articles.title: Former First Deputy Chairman of National Security Committee Avazov and ex-Minister of Health Dosmambetov detained
articles.summary: The Military Prosecutor’s Office confirmed the detention of Kurvanbek Avazov and Kanybek Dosmambetov.

articles.title: Germany's Left to start Berlin coalition talks after antisemitism deal
articles.summary: The Left Party agreed measures on antisemitic incidents, clearing a condition set by the Social Democrats and Greens for exploratory talks.

articles.title: European intelligence services weigh possible fallout after German ex-spy chief's arrest
articles.summary: Intelligence officials said European agencies were assessing whether former BND chief August Hanning had compromised secret information.

articles.title: US imposes fresh sanctions on Iran's shadow fleet
articles.summary: The US Treasury said the measures covered individuals, networks and 17 vessels carrying Iranian crude, oil products and petrochemicals.

articles.title: EXCLUSIVE: Lebanon's Hezbollah gets $200 million from Iran to help displaced, sources say
articles.summary: Sources said the funds were intended for about 50,000 families displaced by the conflict with Israel.

articles.title: Syria weighs military aid for Saudi Arabia amid Yemen war, sources say
articles.summary: A US official and a Syrian military official said the proposal involved possible support against the Houthis in Yemen.

articles.title: EXCLUSIVE: US, Russia explore gas sale to Europe amid Ukraine war, say sources
articles.summary: Five people familiar with the discussions said officials had considered bringing a US investor into the Nord Stream pipelines that previously supplied Germany.

articles.title: EU Commission floats safeguards against democratic backsliding by new members
articles.summary: One proposed measure would allow members to suspend a new member’s voting rights during its first 15 years if it ceased to uphold EU values.
